Vlatko Andonovski built it, Chris Armas finished it: KC Current's NWSL title was continuity through disruption

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1448 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, WASHINGTON, D.C.
  • There was a trademark sense of inevitability that usually follows a team en route to victory, the Current dictating the game state and never looking back against the Spirit.
  • There was a disruptive quality to their run to the championship, one that is inherently rooted in a decision to distance the architect of the project from the project itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Kansas City Current were built to experience a confetti shower, one they undoubtedly felt was not a moment too soon, even if it came a year later than expected. It is hard not to view their first-ever NWSL Championship, which came via a 2-1 win over the Washington Spirit on Saturday, as a continuation of last year's record-breaking Shield triumph and their consistency in recent years, boasting the most cumulative points out of any team in the last three seasons.

There was a trademark sense of inevitability that usually follows a team en route to victory, the Current dictating the game state and never looking back against the Spirit. This, though, was not a year of continuity for the Current.

There was a disruptive quality to their run to the championship, one that is inherently rooted in a decision to distance the architect of the project from the project itself. Chris Armas inherited a team built by Vlatko Andonovski, who first shifted to a sporting director role at the start of the season and then abruptly left in late summer in a move that inspired a wave of emotions from a squad that started to look like a title contender when Andonovski took charge in 2024. Armas began to work with a team that was already capable of winning a title and will be credited with seeing the vision through, all while putting his own spin on things. He also inherited a perfect set of circumstances, which ultimately got the Current over the finish line.

"I walked into a really good team," Armas said post-match. "There was a good culture built in. There was a lot of good pieces and that was one of the reasons that lured me to the club … My job as the head coach is just to try to assess the situation and through tough times help us be steady.".

In a recent development, the Current won eight straight games to close out the season, a run in which they were at their best because they were at their strongest. Their championship-winning season can ultimately be split in two – the stretch of the season in which Temwa Chawinga, Michelle Cooper and Croix Bethune were all fit and available and the stretch of the season in which at least one was missing. It is understandable that the Current would rely on a trio like that one, especially as Bethune became a finishing touch of sorts when she arrived last winter. By design, the group was always going to bolster the Current's chances of going the distance.

"I'm relying on these amazing people and players to help keep things steady but we have talent all along," Armas continued. "We just had to get everyone back and healthy and then we knew we'd have a chance. The question would be, would we have enough time? And we had time, and they did the rest. We stayed steady. We have a great team and we peaked at the right time and now they're champions.".

Recent findings suggest that their overreliance on them, though, did not matter when the business end of the season came. The Current's starry trio was ready; by default, so were the Current.

Armas' team is distinct from Andonovski's in several ways, as evidenced in the NWSL's most glittery moment of the season. Vanessa DiBernardo's olimpico opened the scoring in the second half was the most stylish way of the Current's increased emphasis on set pieces since Armas took over, a skill that was also incredibly useful in their semifinal win at Gotham FC.

Industry observers note that VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

"Lucas Rodriguez has been here from the literal day one," captain Lo'eau LaBonta noted about set piece coach Lucas Rodriguez. "We have been talking about it for the last couple weeks, where we started and where we are now and, so, also that first year, it was his first time ever in women's soccer, so he's grown with the game as well, and he's learned the league and I think that's absolutely what helped him create these amazing set pieces to help us win the trophy.".

Recent findings suggest that the vestiges of Andonovski's team, though, are hard to miss. The journey that led them to Saturday's win was essentially a direct response to the NWSL Shield win that Andonovski oversaw a year ago, a race that was complete by the end of September, a whole month between their trophy lift and their 2025 quarterfinal defeat to Gotham.

Sources indicate that "I think we needed to lose in those quarters almost to lift the trophy and win it all this year because it was just different," captain Lo'eau LaBonta said. "We won the Shield so early last year that we never really had that playoff mentality going into the playoffs because we had already been in it for so long so now that we've experienced everything on each side, I think we absolutely are going to use this to hopefully get help us going forward and make a legacy.".

It is not a pattern that is unfamiliar in Armas' career, either. Saturday's championship is the first major title he collected as a coach since 2018, when he led MLS' Latest York Red Bulls to the Supporters' Shield. Though he was an assistant for several years in the build-up, he also inherited that team from Jesse Marsch, who left midseason for the start of an up-and-down coaching stint in Europe that began at Red Bull Salzburg. The success became hard to replicate; the Red Bulls finished sixth in 2019 and again in 2020, though Armas was out of a job before the season was up. He only managed a few months at Toronto FC, had his own adventures as an assistant coach in England with Ralf Rangnick's Manchester United and at the end of Marsch's ill-fated spell at Leeds United, and then led the Colorado Rapids to a seventh-place finish in 2024 and missed the playoffs in 2025.

Armas' Current exist in a fascinating in-between when it comes to the mold of championship-winning teams. They created a game state that rattled the Spirit from start to finish for the most part, notably doing so while staying true to the attacking identity Andonovski established. The key was creating a physical game state, one that they trialed at Gotham a week earlier and then turned the dial up on at the Spirit on Saturday. The strategy worked – they limited the Spirit to just 0.77 expected goals from 18 shots, all while generating 2.32 from their 15.

According to recent reports, "We are a physical team and there was a lot of whistles and a kind of disruptive play but at the end of the day, we do want to be disruptors so it doesn't matter," defender Kayla Sharples said. "We're going to keep that aggression. I think that's what we did and so we tried not to let it faze us. If anything, it kind of got us more hyped. We need to stay focused and have that mentality finishing off the game.".

In a recent development, there's also the belief that championship-winning teams are often defined by their ability to survive in imperfect circumstances. Their record with and without their starry trio indicates one thing but with winners' medals around their necks, the Current's players believe they managed to strike the best of both worlds approach in order to win on Saturday. Time will tell if Armas can actually extend his streak, something he was unable to do at the Red Bulls. There were undoubtedly moments of adversity along the way, though, their playoff hopes far from a guarantee with five games left in the regular season and a consistency that at least resembles the 2025 Shield-winning campaign will be key in 2027.

Industry observers note that "We kind of have the same style of play but I think Chris has done a great job being the fuel and the fire, making sure we're emphasizing certain details," Sharples noted. "I think what we went through this year, where we learned a lot about resiliency and grit and we were down goals, we went and we came back to win and that's what you need in order to be successful at the end of the season, so I think that was, honestly, the big takeaway from the season, and it really helped us at the end of the day.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.
  • That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning challenges at Stamford Bridge...

Chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

In a recent development, we know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form.

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games.

This morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

According to recent reports, like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

Industry observers note that every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

According to recent reports, let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

Anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

Believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge.

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

In a recent development, he’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Recent findings suggest that which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

Recent findings suggest that for me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck.

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

Striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

According to recent reports, we have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

Emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Recent findings suggest that not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

Alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities.

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Industry observers note that gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • --  For more than a decade, Vanessa DiBernardo has known what it feels like to stand on the doorstep of an NWSL championship.

  • The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON. D.C. --  For more than a decade, Vanessa DiBernardo has known what it feels like to stand on the doorstep of an NWSL championship. On Saturday night at Audi Field, in the 54th minute of the 2026 title game, she finally walked through the door.

Industry observers note that the Kansas City Current midfielder scored the opening goal of the 2026 NWSL Championship on an olimpico, a goal scored from the corner flag. The goal changed the trajectory of the match. Debinha's impact off the bench extended the lead to two, and the team hung on during a stoppage-time surge by the Washington Spirit for a 2-1 victory.

The Naperville, Illinois, native stepped up shortly after halftime when the team won a corner kick, and her service from the left side curled over the leaps of her teammates and defenders and over the outstretched hands of Washington Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver into the back of the net.

Her goal was scored on the biggest stage in the league and broke a scoreless deadlock in a brutally physical game up to that point.

Recent findings suggest that VANESSA DIBERNARDO SCORES AN OLIMPICO IN THE NWSL CHAMPIONSHIP TO PUT KC CURRENT IN FRONT 🤯Stream all the @nwsl championship action on @cbs and @paramountplus. pic.twitter.com/dcZTivEoNt.

Sources indicate that "Yeah, this team was really special. I think there's been just a major journey that we went on through the entire year, and I think it's just even more special to end this way. I'm super grateful to just be a part of this group of girls and staff. It just felt like such a family. So yeah, grateful," DiBernardo stated after the game.

Sources indicate that it's hard to look past the player's use of the past tense. The 34-year-old's contract expires at the end of the season, and the Current have not unveiled an extension, nor has DiBernardo discussed retirement. The player returned to the team from maternity leave in July, following the birth of her daughter Charlie Mae in January.

The veteran's spectacular goal is all the more special because of that return and her relentless effort to reach the league's mountaintop, and it's a moment for a league veteran who's been trying to lift the NWSL trophy for over a decade.

Sources indicate that diBernardo has been playing in the NWSL since its second year. The University of Illinois product was drafted in 2014 by her hometown club, Chicago Stars FC (then Red Stars). She's made several appearances in the NWSL postseason, including five consecutive semifinal appearances through 2019 and a runner-up finish in 2019, before COVID-19 impacted the 2020 regular season.

Even then, during the inaugural Challenge Cup, originally a placeholder for the regular season, she helped the team reach the final, where it fell short against the Houston Dash.

According to recent reports, she reached the NWSL Championship final once again in 2021 with the Stars, mostly playing the season as a defensive midfielder after years of being an attacking midfielder, but ultimately had to exit the game due to injury as Chicago lost another final to the Washington Spirit. That made four straight playoff years of falling one round short of the final, followed by three consecutive losses in finals. By then, she had logged more playoff minutes than almost anyone in league history, and none of them had ended with a trophy.

It has been revealed that the 2021 NWSL Championship would be her final marquee event appearance until she signed with Kansas City in 2022 and reached the 2024 NWSL semifinals with the club. She was on maternity leave the following year when the Current claimed the 2025 NWSL Shield.

Teammate Kayla Sharples has played with DiBernardo for years. Sharples was a rookie with Chicago in 2019, and the duo were teammates through 2021 and reunited in Kansas City when Sharples was traded there in 2023.

"I think Vanessa is a really great leader on this team, and we have a lot of leaders on this team, but she kind of showcases that in different ways. And so for Vanessa, she might not be the most vocal, but she demonstrates it by showing up to training consistently, her quality of play, and just she just shows by example, honestly. And so when you see that, we have a lot of young people on the team, you strive to be like Vanessa," Sharples mentioned after the game.

"She's so amazing. The way that she bounced back, and worked so hard from pregnancy, and she didn't miss a beat. Like she is killing it out there, much deserved for the MVP. I'm really happy for her. And we love her baby Charlie. She always brings the best vibe. She's crawling pregame, like we just love all of that, and so yeah, I'm just really, really happy for her," she mentioned.

It has been revealed that diBernardo's journey in the league is long, and even now, 12 years later, there will be casual viewers who are learning about her for the first time. They'll discover that she won the 2012 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup alongside other legends in Julie Ertz, Sam Mewis, Morgan Gautrat and Crystal Dunn. A crowded U.S. women's national team midfield likely kept her from ever earning a senior-level cap, despite camp call-ups in 2013 and 2019. But she, too, would be destined for more titles; the path there would just look a little different.

She's a concrete example of what domestic success can sometimes look like. Play among and with the greats, and still find yourself on the outside looking in. But not anymore, after lifting the 2025 NWSL Shield and now the NWSL Championship trophy with Kansas City.

Recent findings suggest that "Vanessa DiBernardo is one of the best players to ever play in this league, and she has proved that time and time again. And somehow came back even stronger after having a baby," said KC teammate and NWSL Players Association president Haley Hopkins.

"Seeing her celebrate with her child and celebrate with us, and come back and be that championship MVP. There's no one like her. She's an absolute superstar. Love her, biggest fan," Hopkins remarked.

Industry observers note that along the way, DiBernardo had a playoff record that was already historic. Heading into the semifinals, she had 13 career playoff appearances and 13 starts, with 1,134 playoff minutes, good for third on the all-time list. She is one of just eight players in league history to have converted a penalty in the playoffs, excluding shootouts. But along with playoff pedigree, it's her work ethic and leadership that have been praised the most over the years.

According to recent reports, "For me, yes, I wear the captain's band, but Vanessa is just as much of a captain. She is a leader in all rights. She understands the game. She's like a tactical, technical, genius as well. She knows both sides. She can communicate to people where to go. So, it's so easy for me to be in there because I know what she wants. I know what she needs from me, and it's so easy to follow her lead," stated team captain Lo'eau LaBonta.

"There's been a lot of interview questions, I think, especially on media day the other day, it was like, 'what was the turning point?' And I don't know if that was the turning point when she was back, but it definitely helped us have some consistency and solidarity. So she means everything ... We look to her all the time, and that olimpico? That was saucy. And you know, there's moments of brilliance like that when the teams are out there just kicking the crap out of each other, so shout out to her. MVP for sure," LaBonta said.

Industry observers note that maybe this year was supposed to be harder, but DiBernardo's demeanor never really indicated that. Longevity feels like a rarity now in an NWSL that's getting younger, with play that's quicker and more transitional than it was when she was drafted in 2014. But her legacy has also helped shape the next wave of superstars, especially those on her team, and it'll continue to evolve no matter what she does next.

Sources indicate that "I feel like being a veteran in this league is special. I think this league is really unique in the style of play; that is, kind of, every game is intense. So, whether that's just being vocal, but also just like being calm on the ball, or slowing the game down, or there's just so many moments in a game that you can contribute," DiBernardo said.

"I think the veterans in this league have kind of grown with it. So, it's fun to see the young players come into this league and kind of help them guide them, but they're bringing their own flair, and it's fun to see, and it's just growing the league," she said.

Calm on the ball, a leader in her play and now a mother, DiBernardo approached her return to play just like her soccer: a step and a touch, with plenty of patience.

It has been revealed that "I think I just kind of took my journey one step at a time. I knew it was going to be difficult to kind of get back to who I was as a player, and I knew I was going to be different as a person. But I feel like our team gave me so much grace and time to be able to do that," DiBernardo said.

"It was really special to kind of go through my pregnancy, but also my return to play with this group of people, and to kind of get to share the moment all together," she said.

In a recent development, for DiBernardo, who lost to the Spirit in the 2021 final, Saturday's goal and the team's victory feel like everything had always been leading to this moment. It took 13 years, two clubs, eight semifinal appearances, three lost finals and a year away from the game as she became a new mom, but Vanessa DiBernardo is an NWSL Championship winner.

Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.
  • "There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak remarked after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.
  • "The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak remarked after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, stated in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it noted the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

On November 8, Norway said it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, stated Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

Sources indicate that the thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

For now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brian Brobbey only played for 67 minutes but, in that time, he collected a yellow card, ripped Levi Colwill’s shirt and earned himself a standing ovation after morphing into a battering ram.
  • Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said there was nobody like the Netherlands striker in the Premier League and it said everything that everyone wanted to make Brobbey centre of attention after a long overdue home win, even though he had not scored.
  • According to recent reports, “No, he’s not unstoppable,” Chelsea’s head coach replied when asked why his team had found Brobbey too much to handle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Talk about cramming everything in. Brian Brobbey only played for 67 minutes but, in that time, he collected a yellow card, ripped Levi Colwill’s shirt and earned himself a standing ovation after morphing into a battering ram.

Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said there was nobody like the Netherlands striker in the Premier League and it said everything that everyone wanted to make Brobbey centre of attention after a long overdue home win, even though he had not scored. Everyone, that is, bar Xabi Alonso.

According to recent reports, “No, he’s not unstoppable,” Chelsea’s head coach replied when asked why his team had found Brobbey too much to handle. “He’s stoppable – but only when you defend better than we did. We were not bullied. We didn’t produce enough.”.

That is one way of putting it. Another would be to say Brobbey was everything that Chelsea, much to Alonso’s disgust, were not: a bristling menace, a steamroller wearing a pair of boots, a player on a mission to help transform the mood – Enzo Le Fée’s decisive spot kick owed everything to Brobbey.

Chelsea arrived on Wearside looking to establish themselves in the top four ahead of the break but, instead, Alonso watched through his fingers as Sunderland reminded everyone why they were the joyous story of last season, a beautiful mix of inspiration and perspiration.

In fairness to the Chelsea manager, he refused to get caught in the minutiae of contentious penalty decisions – one that Chelsea were denied, another that they conceded – and could only lament as Sunderland ground out their first Premier League win since August 30, 70 long days ago.

“It wasn’t the best game,” Alonso noted. “I think that we didn’t deserve more than probably one point, maybe. We need to be more consistent on the move, to get the ball from one side to the other, and we didn’t do that good enough. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.”.

Sources indicate that unlike Sunderland. If you had turned up at the Stadium of Light without looking at the Premier League table, you would not have believed the hosts were bottom and you would not have given credence to the idea Le Bris, who has worked miracles these past two years, was under pressure.

In a recent development, things, however, could not have started worse for Le Bris. Though Granit Xhaka has not shown last season’s form in these challenging opening months, the game proposal was built around him, so to see the Sunderland captain hobbling off after three minutes was symptomatic of how things have gone for the Wearsiders.

It has been revealed that “He felt something in the final sprint of the warm-up,” Le Bris explained. “We don’t know how bad it is.”.

According to recent reports, he is not the kind of coach, though, who will bemoan bad fortune. Le Bris sent on Jules Ahoka to replace Xhaka and watched as he, along with colleagues in red and white, set about trampling all over Chelsea’s intentions with incessant hard work.

Yet there was more to it. Sunderland can play, either intricately or directly, and a lovely move in the 12th minute needed a desperate, sliding intervention from Pep Chavarría’s to stop Trai Hume’s volley sliding in at the far post.

In the next attack, another Chemsdine Talbi cross – the Moroccan having been found by a peach of a pass from goalkeeper Robin Roefs – invited Brobbey to inflict maximum damage, but the Dutchman made a hash of his opportunity.

It has been revealed that so close for Brobbey! 🤏 Sunderland almost take the lead against Chelsea. https://t.co/CUE6jHbPH2.

The momentum could have changed completely in the 23rd minute. Alonso, his players and staff were convinced they would be given a penalty after Cole Palmer tumbled when his legs tangled with Luke O’Nien but, after a lengthy delay, VAR Nick Hopton felt there was no case to answer.

Sources indicate that hopton was involved again in the 33rd minute but, as Alonso noted, Chelsea only had themselves to blame. Colwill simply could not contain Brobbey when he began marauding, grappling, grabbing and clipping the Dutchman’s heels. Le Fée did the rest, sending Mike Penders the wrong way.

In a recent development, enzo Le Fee dispatches the penalty as Sunderland take the lead against Chelsea! 🔴⚪️ https://t.co/cCtYsHVWB9.

Industry observers note that from that point, Chelsea were in trouble, no matter how many changes Alonso made. They huffed, puffed, but nothing worked. They had come up against a red-and-white wall, fortified by constant backing from the stands, and the west Londoners were never going to knock it down.

One incident, as the clock ticked towards 90 minutes, encapsulated everything good about this Sunderland display when O’Nien chased down substitute Geovany Quenda to make a challenge. Another moment of defending from Thomas Meunier on Morgan Rogers was exceptional.

Recent findings suggest that “You could see our identity and our togetherness and the way we managed the game,” mentioned Le Bris, who was booked when hectoring referee Jarred Gillett. “These three points were critical. It was a struggle at times to manage situations. We highlighted as a group real heart.”.

It has been revealed that and nobody did that more than Brobbey. No wonder Le Bris will be hoping Xavi Hernández, the Netherlands head coach, handles him with care over the next 10 days. On this form, he will be the fuel that drives Sunderland’s quest for survival.

It has been revealed that “You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight. We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control. With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces.”.

On where Chelsea stand ahead of the international break...

Industry observers note that “How you do – good or not – it is a matter of staying together. The international break is coming so the lads can be calm in the head and when we all come back we need to be motivated to go again.”.

“For me it wasn’t a penalty. He barely touched him, I think it was the other way round. He grabbed him.”.

They cannot make anything of set piece and Sunderland have the three points - it wasn’t pretty but they needed the three points and edged the contest.

Questions will be asked of Chelsea now, they were bullied in the first-half and weren’t able to create anything in the second.

In a recent development, so close for Brobbey! 🤏 Sunderland almost take the lead against Chelsea. https://t.co/CUE6jHbPH2.

According to recent reports, the half ends with an audacious attempt at goal from Rogers, a full 40 yards out from a free kick. It’s catching practice for Roefs and that sums up Chelsea as an attacking force in the first 45. Sunderland are well worth their lead.

It has been revealed that rogers has a shot-cum-cross from the left and it sails high, wide and not so handsome. He’s been on the periphery this half, as has Palmer and that explains as much as anything why they are behind. Sunderland have cut out the supply to him and Roefs has had little to do as a result.

It has been revealed that approaching half-time and save for the contentious VAR call when he wanted a penalty, Cole Palmer has done absolutely nothing. The talk of him being in the England squad, on this evidence, is for the birds. Sunderland are full value for their half-time lead. Chelsea, like Palmer, have been absolutely insipid.

There will be five minutes added time in this first half.

Something I’ve not written much this half ‘chance for Chelsea’. Neto works a bit of space in the inside-right channel outside the box, but his shot is easily saved by Roefs.

Talbi attacks down the left but cuts in when he would have been better served going wide.

Sources indicate that chelsea have seen plenty of the ball but they’ve been way too slow and cumbersome with it. It’s been in front of the Sunderland back lines and easy to defend against. The hosts are letting the visitors have the ball wide and with Neto in the middle, it’s been too easy for Le Bris’s men.

Sources indicate that brobbey wants the ball at every opportunity and Sunderland would be well advised to give it to him. Colwill is has his hands full.

Recent findings suggest that sunderland have kept the aggression and energy throughout the half - and kept Chelsea quiet as a result. As I type that the hosts give Lavia too much room 25 yards out and his shot is well wide of the left-hand post.

The lead is no more than Sunderland deserve and that means, as the table stands, Manchester United are bottom of the Premier League. Fair play to Enzo Le Fee for keeping his nerve in a pressure situation. Sunderland needed him to be cool.

It has been revealed that they’ve deserved that, they’ve been the better side and are well worth the lead. Le Fee sends Penders the wrong way, burying the ball into the bottom left corner.

According to recent reports, brobbey has been a handful (as he always is) and Colwill brings the SUBSTANTIAL (yes, caps lock and bold are necessary) Dutchman down in the box. It looks as though it was six of one and hald a dozen of the other, but the spotkick stands.

In a recent development, ahoka has impressed since coming on, his nifty footwork helps win Sunderland a throw in the final third. Mukiele has a substantial thrown on him but it does not result in a chance. Still, this is good from the hosts and Chelsea are second best at the moment. They were in the first half against United last week, and ended up winning so...

Recent findings suggest that another chance for Sunderland as Brobbey bullies Colwill on the halfway line before driving at Fofana. He gets to the edge of the area, beats the Chelsea defender before his shot goes wide. The last touch took him too wide, but again, promising signs for the hosts.

Early days this, of course, but Sunderland absolutely do not look like a team that is currently the worst in the Premier League. They should have the lead here but Brian Brobbey’s miss from six yards is indicative of how things have been going.

It has been revealed that sunderland are being aggressive, they need to be and it’s a contrast from the previous month. With that approach, however, comes risks and Mukiele gives away a free-kick inside his own half. Luckily for him, nothing comes from the set-piece.

Recent findings suggest that first chance of the game for Chelsea and, as with Brobbey 10 minutes ago, it should have found the back of the net. Rogers is the culprit - he sends his header wide of the right post after a grade-A cross from Palestra.

One-all in terms of great chances...but the score remains 0-0.

Recent findings suggest that palmer is bundled over on the outskirts of the area and he and Chelsea players appeal for something - could be a free-kick of penalty...the referee is having nothing of it. The replay suggests he may well have been hard done by but VAR also is having nothing of it...it was a foul as none of the marauding Sunderland players, O’Nien among them (obviously), got the ball and most definitely got Palmer...think the hosts got away with that one.

Recent findings suggest that yellow card for Ahoka for a foul on Caicado, he may need to walk a tightrope for the rest of the match. But it’s an illustration of the energy and purpose with which Sunderland have approached this match.

Sunderland have looked the better side so far and have had the better chances.

Sources indicate that better from Chelsea in the sense that they controlled the game for two minutes. Lots of good, neat passing but no end product, it’s all in front of a composed Sunderland defence.

Another good chance for Sunderland and once again Talbi proves his worth. He cuts back onto his right and delivers a peach of a cross from the left. Brobbey gets in front of his man and all he has to do is hit the target...alas his first-time shot goes wide. That should be 1-0 to the hosts who are the better side at the moment.

Industry observers note that good from Sunderland who look so much more energetic than at any point during their previous few matches. Ahoka does well in the middle before freeing Talbi down the left. The Moroccan gets in a cross and Le Fee’s shot is blocked. Promising signs for the hosts.

It has been revealed that what a blow this is for Regis Le Bris. Less than two minutes gone and Granit Xhaka is having to leave the pitch with an obvious injury. Some fans around the press box booed Xhaka as he was hobbling off - is that a hangover from his attempts to move to Chelsea? - but on afternoon when Le Bris needed everything to go his way, he’s already on the back foot.

According to recent reports, neto is in the Sunderland half but three Sunderland players snap at his heels like a hyperactive dog after a bone. Chelsea haven’t been allowed to settle yet. Plenty of time to go though...

It has been revealed that sunderland are looking to find Brobbey at every opportunity, but Chelsea’s backline intercept well. Nothing of note created so far, but the hosts are on the front foot, which is what they and the fans needed.

Sunderland attack down the right with Meunier, nothing comes of it but the hosts look as though they mean business here. A minute later Sadiki and Brobbey nearly combine to create something. Close but no cigar...

Bad news for Sunderland, Xhaka is down and it looks as though he may well have to come off...oh dear. While he’s not been at his best this season he’s still the man the side looks towards for inspiration (an boy do they need that is dollops today...)...and, indeed he is forced off. Ahoka, who is highly rated but raw replaces him. The Congolese player now has a big chance to make a name for himself.

Chelsea with the early possession, but they go backwards and the hosts are up and at them with the press and the visitors have to go back to Penders in goal.

They’re under way at the Stadium of Light, Sunderland are in their famous red and white and Chelsea in their away outfit of black shirts and shorts and yelow socks.

As the Stadium of Light remembers all those who lost their lives in war.

The Last Post is played and the minute’s silence is impeccably observed.

Warming-up in our Remembrance shirt ❤️ https://t.co/aTB8sfdLKP.

And we’re moments away from kick-off in the North East.

It has been revealed that this is a big afternoon for both teams. It will be an emotional one, too, for Jordan Henderson, who started his career at Sunderland many years ago. Xabi Alonso has confirmed he has been picked because of the quality he provides, rather than any sentimental value, and Regis Le Bris revealed ahead of the fixture he tried to bring the England international home during the summer window, when Chelsea attempted to sign Granit Xhaka.

In a recent development, “Jordan is a great player, first of all,” said Le Bris. “For the connection with the club, it’s not my part. It was with Flo [Ghisolfi, director of football] and Kyril [Louis-Dreyfus, the Sunderland owner], they had conversations.

“I thought that it could have been a good signing for the club, a good symbol, a great player, a great leader. But the market is the market.”.

Recent findings suggest that has just stated that Sunderland, and in particular Brian Brobbey, can ‘get at’ the Chelsea defence of Palestra, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria. I am not sure he has seen much of the Sunderland attack this year, but Brobbey is a handful for any defence.

On how to improve the sorry form...

“We have to stay consistent and true to our identity. It’s always difficult to predict what the other side does but you have to focus on yourself and connect with the fans and impose our ideas.”.

On whether they can get a result today...

Recent findings suggest that “I hope so... I see the players every day, they care and sometime its hard to understand the unforced errors.”.

On Talbi returning to the XI...

“He’s loved by fans and team, so we know the situation at beginning of season. He is an notable player for us and didn’t start for various reasons, but has qualities run in behind and finish - he’s excited worked and has worked hard.”.

According to recent reports, I mentioned earlier that Sunderland did the double over Chelsea last season. But the manner of the victories revealed more than the scorelines. In both matches, especially the second, the west Londoners looked somewhat lightweight and easily bullied.

This season Xabi Alonso has been determined to ensure that that is not the case this season.

In the land of the Premier League giants, Chelsea have been on the small side in recent seasons. But they are no longer being looked down upon and are finally showing signs of being capable of going toe-to-toe physically with opponents.

Sunday’s opponents Sunderland ran Chelsea off the park twice last season. Only once, in the 36th Premier League game of the campaign against Liverpool, did Chelsea cover more distance than their opposition.

Here’s Matt Law’s article on Why Chelsea have gone from pint-sized players to taller trees...

SUNDERLAND XI TO FACE CHELSEA: Roefs, Meunier, Mukiele, O’Nein, Reinildo, Xhaka, Hume, Le Fee, Talbi, Brobbey.

Subs: Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Rigg, Tutierov, Ahoka, Fofana, Angulo, Isador.

Regis Le Bris makes two changes from the sorry defeat at Coventry City. Nordi Mukiele returns to the centre of defence and there’s a start for Chemsdine Talbi  – Chris Rigg and Nilson Angulo are the ones to make way.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE SUNDERLAND: Penders, Palestra, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria, Henderson, Lavia, Caicedo, Neto, Palmer, Rogers.

Subs: Sharman-Lowe, Gusto, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli, Barco, Quenda, Estevao, Welbeck, Emegha.

Xabi Alonso also makes two changes – Pep Chavarria and Jordan Henderson start today. Estevao Willian drops to the bench while Josh Acheampong is a somewhat surprise absence the 20.

Goalkeeper Mike Penders continues in goal with Emiliano Martinez deemed not ready to return having fractured his jaw against Everton.

That Sunderland did the double over Chelsea last season.

A last-minute winner from Chemsdine Talbi grabbed the points at Stamford Bridge, before Sunderland won 2-1, without breaking sweat, at the Stadium of Light on the last day of the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that those victories, and the manner of them, underlined what a season it was for Regis Le Bris’s men. How they wish this campaign started as that one ended.

Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

According to recent reports, the hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume noted.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”.
